links.reason: Both turn on the bangles that will not stay (இருகையும் நில்லா வளை; இறைஇறவா நின்ற வளை) when the shore lord leaves, a stock sign of separation. A conditional in another poem (புல்லான் விடினே) cannot fix the tense of துறந்தமை in the Kural, so the teaches sentence borrows the reading it claims to support.

Both argue from death's unpredictability (உறன்முறை மரபிற் கூற்றம் ... நாளும்; நாச்செற்று விக்குள்மேல் வாராமுன்) to acting now. Staying with her instead of going after wealth (ஆள்வினை மருங்கிற் பிரியார்) does not contradict hastening to good deeds, so 'opposite conduct' overstates; it is the same urgency in another domain.

On a plain reading இன்பம் விழையான் (628) and இன்பம் பயக்கும் வினை (669) pull apart, and both accept pain, so the tension is real but surface. The teaches sentence only concedes a scope difference and teaches nothing from the pair.

Natrinai 212 sets the bards' strings (நரம்பொடு கொள்ளும்) beside the child's sweet voice (இன் குரல்) that makes the mother anxious (அவவுக் கொள் மனத்தேம்), which gives a real echo of the Kural's flute and lute against children's prattle. The point that the sweetness turns to pain in the father's absence holds, but the claim that the Kural 'assumes the father present' is thin.

Both set காமம் against நாண். Whose காமம் has 'killed shame and gone far' in Kuruntokai 231 is not fixed: after காணாக் கழிப மன்னே it can be his former love that has now gone far from her, not her own desire. The teaches sentence builds on one reading of a contested line.
links.text_issue: line 6 கணியிற் where the sense wants கணையின் 'arrow'

links.reason: Both counsel giving because death is certain (நினக்கும் வருதல் வைகல் அற்றே; இழைத்தநாள் எல்லை இகவா). The difference in motive is real: Purananuru 359 offers fame (ஈண்டுநீடு விளங்கும் ... புகழே) and the Naladiyar only the nearness of the drum. But one quatrain cannot show that 'the later book drops the reward', and the pair is mainly a shared counsel, not a qualification.

Kalittokai 27 likens the riverbank trees to the wealth of a just giver (ஈதலில் குறை காட்டாது ... தீது இலான் செல்வம் போல் தீம் கரை மரம் நந்த), the exact inverse of Kural 216's பயன்மரம் ... செல்வம். The reversed direction of a distinctive figure is a real and specific observation.

Ainkurunuru 142 resolves உள்ளேன் ... படீஇயர் என் கண்ணே, not-thinking as a chosen cure for sleeplessness; Kural 1207 says மறப்பறியேன் and that even உள்ளினும் உள்ளம் சுடும். The shared verb உள் makes the conflict exact: one woman claims a power the other denies.

There is a good verbal hinge: the Paripadal's கரவா வழக்கிற்று against the friend's கரத்தல் கூடுமோ in Akananuru 296, both on Vaigai bathing. But the Paripadal lines are obscure (lines 66 to 67 and 71; what கரவா governs, perhaps அம்பி), so the 'custom with nothing hidden' on which the teaches rests is itself uncertain.
links.text_issue: lines 62-73: line 64 flagged as a possible dropped heading; lines 66-67, 71-73 obscure in construction

links.reason: The Naladiyar's மன்னா மகிழ்ச்சி (in its chapter on youth) is set against Ainkurunuru 415's இனிதுடன் கழிக்கின் இளமை இனிதால். The opposition is real, but the Ainkurunuru never states that youth passes, so 'the same premise' is the proposer's, and the pair is the familiar love-versus-renunciation topic.
links.text_issue: line 4 அவர்ப் புணர்வு, third person in a speech to மடந்தை

links.reason: Both have sleepless eyes in separation (பல்லிதழ் உண்கண் பாடொல் லாவே; துஞ்சா). In Kuruntokai 5 the man has already left (பிரிந்தென), so அதுகொல் ... காம நோயே discovers what love-sickness is, not that she is in love; the developmental story in the teaches sentence is constructed.

Natrinai 129's வாழ்தும் என்ப ('he says we shall live' till he returns) meets Kural 1151's வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை on the same verb: both make his promise of return a question of her survival. The midnight thunder heard alone (நடு நாள் யாமத்தும் தமியம் கேட்டே) gives the couplet's irony its scene.

Kar Narpathu 4 calls the season the cure (பசலை மருந்து); Kural 1265 says the pallor goes only after seeing him with full eyes (கண்ணாரக் கண்டபின்). The contrast of sign and sight is real, but the friend's claim is consolation that the season brings him, so the two limit each other more than they conflict, and 'answer to the whole method' overstates.

The connection is real: Evvi's bards (எவ்வி இழந்த வறுமையாழ்ப் பாணர்) in Kuruntokai 19 and Evvi's wounds in Purananuru 233. But Purananuru 233 has no flowerless heads, so this is not a shared image, and nothing in 233 shows a 'recognised mourning custom'; it only reports the wounds and wishes the news false.

Both deploy the night path's beasts (Akananuru 112: bear, tiger; Kurinjippattu 252-259: tiger, bear, elephant, crocodiles, spirits) to press for marriage, one to the man (வரையின் எவனோ) and one, per the thurai அறத்தொடு நிற்றல், toward the mother. The teaches sentence is specific and true, but neither verse limits the other, so 'qualifies' does not fit.

The shared phrase is exact (தம்மில் தமதுண் டன்ன; தம்மில் இருந்து தமதுபாத்து உண்டற்றால்) and a real same_image. But the teaches sentence's conclusion that the image 'belongs to the settled household rather than to secret love' fails: Kural 1107 uses it of the embrace in its own kalavu chapters, and Kuruntokai 83 uses it of jackfruit, not of marriage.

Both end on the same restitution formula, நலம் தந்து சென்மே, with the beauty likened to a Chera town (கடல் கெழு மாந்தை with குட்டுவன் in the same poem; குட்டுவன் மரந்தை). One speaker is a courtesan, the other a friend whose thurai is வரைவு கடாயது, so the shift of the formula into a demand for marriage is shown by the texts.

Konrai as gold ornament (காசி னன்ன போது; கழலாகிப் பொன்வட்டாய்) is a stock likeness, and the venba does not take it from Kuruntokai 148. The venba's sense is uncertain; நீயும் பிறரொடும்காண் calls witnesses, but that it 'expands that single likeness' into proof is the proposer's construction.

Paripadal 1 says திங்களும் ... கனலியும் நீ, identity; Paripadal 4 says நின் வெம்மையும் விளக்கமும் ஞாயிற்று உள and that things came about நிற் பிரிந்து, a sharing out of his qualities. The two forms of praise genuinely limit each other within one collection.
links.text_issue: paripadal 4 line 25 flagged as a possible dropped heading

links.reason: நீடுதோறு இனியர் and புரையோர் கேண்மை in Natrinai 1 match Kural 783's பயில்தொறும் ... பண்புடையாளர் தொடர்பு, sweetness growing with acquaintance of the noble. That the heroine argues from that maxim to his not leaving (செய்பு அறியலரே) is what the pair shows; only 'the Kural's rule' implies a borrowing the texts do not prove.

Both rest on love across births (மறுமை யுலகத்து மன்னுதல் பெறுமே; இம்மைப் பிறப்பில் பிரியலம்), a real link. But the Kural's joke needs only the belief in rebirth, not 'Paranar's belief'; the claim that it 'works only because' of this convention overreaches.

Paripadal 1's opening gives the plough-bearer's emblems (வால் வளை மேனி, நாஞ்சில், ஒரு குழை ஒருவனை) to the one god addressed, while Paripadal 2 names the conch-white, palmyra-bannered brother apart and lets the god be younger or elder as the worshipper says (இளையன் என்போர்க்கு இளையை). The pairing does show a known two-brother story behind the first song's fusion.
links.text_issue: both spans flagged uncertain; Paripadal 1 line 4 வேழம் not secure

links.reason: Both have the friend speak for an overhearing man (சிறைப்புறம்) as the millet ripens for the parrots, and both turn on the mother's look (என் முகம் நோக்கினள்; பல்கால் நோக்கும்). Natrinai 206's open question (செல்வாள் என்றுகொல் செறிப்பல் என்றுகொல்) and Akananuru 302's விடுநள் போலாள் make the look a deadline, as the teaches says.

The girl's eyes acting on the man is a common figure; the fisher's net turned into the eye's net (நுண்வலைப் பரதவர் ... கண்வலைப் படூஉம்) is a different image from the life-eating look (கண்டார் உயிருண்ணும்). The claim that the older poetry gave the Kural's 'abstract killing gaze' a landscape generalises from one poem.

Both measure love by what lies between an embrace: வளியிடை போழப் படாஅ முயக்கு against முயக்கிடை மலைவு, groves where tigers roar. The teaches sentence's reading, that the distance is felt as a gap within the embrace, is specific and grounded in the shared முயக்கு ... இடை.

Natrinai 50 ends on trust without examination (சிறுமை பெருமையின் காணாது துணிந்தே), on the strength of a reputation (செறுநரும் விழையும் செம்மலோன்), matching Kural 508's தேரான் பிறனைத் தெளிந்தான். The parallel is real and specific, but the poem applies the rule in another domain rather than limiting it.

The verbal match is exact (பெருநாண் நீக்கி; நாணினை நீக்கி) with the madal in both. Kuruntokai 182 adds the occasion (தூது ... மெலிந்திலள்) and counts the cost in others' mockery (பிறர் எள்ளத் தோன்றி), which the Kural's general statement omits.

Both fear the night path (கவலை in both), a stock situation. Ainkurunuru 362 is not quite a plea to stop coming: it ends in praise (அருள்புரி நெஞ்சம் உய்த்தர). The claim about what the whole முன்னிலைப் பத்து does is a generalisation from one poem.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 362 colophon thinai பாலை; the marker reads kurinji

links.reason: The two decade poems are formal variations on எந்தோள் துறந்த ... எவன்கொல், and the note is accurate. Reading them as a two-step case, desire then history, imposes a sequence on what the decade form gives as parallel variants.

Both refuse a straying man (எம்மனை இன்றொடு வாரல்; நண்ணேன் பரத்தநின் மார்பு). The Kural calls him பரத்த, so its refusal is not only a 'witty pretext' about looks; the teaches sentence misdescribes the couplet, and the Kainnilai's ground is half lost.
links.text_issue: Kainnilai 38 line 4 lacuna; line 3 துயிலின் obscure

links.reason: Natrinai 17 states the ranking in the Kural's own terms (உயிரினும் சிறந்த நாணும் நனி மறந்து), and Kural 1017 makes it a rule (நாணால் உயிரைத் துறப்பர்). What nearly breaks it is the mother's tenderness (மெல்லிய இனிய கூறலின்), a real limit on the maxim. The Kural's நாண் is a man's sense of honour and hers is a woman's modesty, but the ranking is the same.

Malaipadukadam opens the welcome with the patron's name (விறல்வேள் வயிரியம் எனினே), and the hosts are welcoming in manner (கேளாது கெழீஇ, இனிய கூறி). That is a real contrast with the Kural's householder duty. But Kural 90 is about the host's changed face, which the idyll does not touch, so the hinge is thin.

Ainthinai Aimpathu 14's மாவினவு வார்போல names as a manner of coming exactly the question Akananuru 388's hunter asks (ஒருத்தல் நும் புனத்துழிப் போகல் உறுமோ). The simile shows that the pretext could be named and seen through, as the teaches says.

The shared image is distinctive: a god-made figure on the western face of Kolli (தெய்வம் எழுதிய வினை மாண் பாவை; பூதம் புணர்த்த புதிது இயல் பாவை). The two verses do not make incompatible claims: one beauty 'plots death' (கொலை சூழ்ந்தனள்) when refused and the other makes the path safe (ஏமம்). That is a double-edged image, not a tension.

The hymn's crowd alternates men's and women's attributes, but they are worshippers bearing offerings (மடையர் குடையர் புகையர் பூ ஏந்தி), not lovers in each other's arms. The heaven it names is one of ripened deeds (விளைந்தார் வினையின் விழுப் பயன்). Setting this against Kural 1103's மென்றோள் துயில் stretches a shared mention of Mal's heaven into an answer.
links.text_issue: lines 30-32 obscure; line 32 and 36 repaired; lineation off at line 44

links.reason: Kalittokai 26's refrain (நிழல் சேர்ந்தார்க்கு உலையாது காத்து ஓம்பி ... ஏதில் நாட்டு உறைபவர்) is the praise of Purananuru 22 (வெண் குடை நீழலான் வாள் மருங்கு இலோர் காப்பு உறங்க ... வேறுபுலத்து இறுக்கும் தானை). The woman turns the hero's public virtue against her own neglect, a specific puram-to-akam use.

Both call creatures of the land to the secret union (குருகும் உண்டு; கடுவனும் அறியும்), a real pairing. But who தான் and தன்கண் are in Kuruntokai 26 is uncertain, and that the heron 'saw nothing' is an inference from ஆரல் பார்க்கும். 'Qualifies' does not name the relation.

The shared word மிச்சில் and the hospitality ethic are real. But in Kuruntokai 233 the leftover of offerings is shared with all (யாவர்க்கும் வரைகோள் அறியா), while in Kural 85 the host himself eats the leftover. The claim that the rule was a mark of marriage 'before it was a maxim' is a chronology neither text supports.

The form is fixed in both: girls decking sand-houses (வண்டல் விளக்கயரும்; சிறு மனை அணியும்), then the friend's 'is it fitting' (தகுவதோ; தகுமோ) about the girl's wasting beauty. Natrinai 283's வாய்மை சான்ற நின் சொல் supplies the ground the venba leaves out.

The phrasing is exact: துறைவனொடு இலங்கெயிறு தோன்ற நக்கதன் பயனே against துறைவனொடு ஒருநாள் நக்குவிளையாடலும் கடிந்தன்று. One laugh's cost in 381 and its prohibition in 401 make a real pair. That the household is the forbidder is the natural reading of கடிந்தன்று.

The formula is shared and striking: இன்னா ஆகப் பிறர் மண் கொண்டு / இனிய against தமக்கு இனிது என்று ... பிறர்க்கு இன்னா, with அறன் in both. But in Purananuru 12 the king does not claim it as virtue; the poet asks அறனோ மற்றஇது and gets no answer. The man of Kalittokai 62 alone calls seizing அறன். It is a moral rule applied in war and love, not an image.

Both mock the husband's bard, a stock marutham figure. The teaches sentence says the wife shames the husband 'without naming him', but Ainkurunuru 43's நின்னினும் charges him to his face, and Akananuru 56 names the ஊரன்'s chest as the bard's errand.

Innaa Narpathu 33 counts as painful கள்ளுண்பான் கூறுங் கருமப் பொருள், and Muthumozhikkanchi 63 gives the ground, that a drinker without lapse (சோர்வு இன்மை) is a falsehood. The pair is small but exact: the lapse explains why his business is painful.

Ainkurunuru 24's நலங்கொண்டு துறப்பது (taking her beauty and abandoning) against Kural 1183's கொண்டார் கைம்மாறா நோயும் பசலையும் தந்து: plain taking becomes an exchange. The kin-destroying creatures of அவனூர் give the Sangam charge its force, as the teaches says. The speaker addressing அன்னாய் may be the heroine rather than the friend.

poems.note: The butter image is an open simile (போல) joined to இந்நோய்.
Every natural image is joined to her heart by a refrain (என் ... நெஞ்சம் ... கூம்பும்), so all are open comparisons.
Lines 1-4 are hard to construe (தாழைக் குடம்பை நோனா); the top-like girl is an open simile.
The buffalo grazing the fields and coming home thinking of its calf maps neatly onto the marutham husband, but neither the poem nor a thurai states the situation.
The roosting birds serve as a time phrase in a refrain of evenings; no sense beyond the hour is fixed.
The roar of the salt carts that frightens the heron answers the gossip (அலர்) the friend fears, and the heron's fright the girl's; the thurai names அலர் அச்சம.

iraicchi.act: trumpets because it cannot see its mate sleeping beside it, hidden by mist
iraicchi.sense: With the girl shut in at home (the thurai's செறிப்பு), the man will cry for her unseen though she is near, so he must marry.

poems.note: The mist could be pressed as a second pair (the confinement), which would make it ullurai; taken as one pair of creatures acting.
Lines 1-2 are lost; nothing can be tagged.

vehicle: பொன் நேர் நுண் தாது புன்னை தூஉம்

poems.note: The parrots are the whole poem; striking them leaves nothing.

The neythal cut down unseen by the reapers yet opening to the sun unaware of its harm answers the girl wounded by a careless man and still unaware or trusting; the thurai places it as her reply to consolation.
The killer elephant that broke the young ஆசினி is the hill lord who caused the girl's illness, and the broken tree her wasting, which the velan misreads.
Budding punnai and budding gossip (அலர்) give one match only.

iraicchi.act: climbs the palm frond toward its mate's nest and keeps calling its partner till its life fails
iraicchi.sense: Her own longing calls for him the same way, which is why she cannot hold firm as the friend asks.

poems.note: The egret rushing to see another bird's dead young does act, but what it implies for the lovers (he is a stranger to mother) cannot be said in one sentence.

vehicle: அகில் சுடு கானவன் உவல் சுடு கமழ் புகை

iraicchi.act: the doe with her fawn frolics in the rain on his road
iraicchi.sense: Seeing a mother and young at play he will think of his own home and return.

poems.note: The bull and heifer standing with the herd are a literal detail of going home, not an act set beside the lovers'.

iraicchi.act: the crab stays on the dune with its mate
iraicchi.sense: Even the crab of his shore keeps its mate, while he leaves her friend to pallor.

poems.note: The heron is the addressee-witness of the question; striking it removes the poem's sense.
